scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team blames the fabric -- they say "spine_router_0_0 has failed,
swap the spine". Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device or link to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or
anything beyond. The ticket MISDIRECTS to the fabric / a spine, but the fabric
is healthy: the CLOS fabric is redundant and the OTHER leaf (leaf_router_0_1)
still reaches the fabric normally through both spines, which it could not do if
spine_router_0_0 had failed. The symptom is purely the down access link at
pc_0_0's leaf, not a spine/fabric fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES spine_router_0_0: the
spines and fabric still carry the other leaf, so the user's "spine has failed"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that swaps / blames spine_router_0_0 has followed
the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. spine_router_0_0 / the fabric needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a fabric/spine fault
bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on leaf_router_0_0, not spine_router_0_0. The router's eth2
interface — the directly connected link to pc_0_0 — is in an administratively
or physically DOWN state (kernel flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP
or LOWER_UP). The IP address 10.0.0.1/24 is correctly configured on eth2, but
because the interface has no link, the Linux kernel never installs the
connected route 10.0.0.0/24 into the routing table.

This breaks the system in two ways simultaneously. First, at Layer 2, pc_0_0
(whose eth0 is healthy and UP) cannot exchange any frames with its gateway
because the router-side port is down — all ARP and ICMP packets from pc_0_0
are dropped in hardware. Second, FRR's BGP process has a `network 10.0.0.0/24`
statement configured to advertise pc_0_0's subnet across the fabric, but
because the prefix is absent from the RIB (no connected route), the import-
check fails silently and the advertisement is never generated. Confirmed via
`show bgp … advertised-routes`: leaf_router_0_0 sends only 10.0.1.0/24
(a received route) to its spine peers, never its own local /24. As a result,
every other device in the fabric — both spines, super_spine, and
leaf_router_0_1 — has no route to 10.0.0.0/24, making pc_0_0 unreachable
from anywhere.

Both spine_router_0_0 and spine_router_0_1 are fully operational with
established BGP sessions and correct forwarding tables.

Root cause: leaf_router_0_0's eth2 interface is down, severing the L2 link to
pc_0_0 and preventing the 10.0.0.0/24 prefix from entering the RIB or being
BGP-advertised to the fabric.

Corrective fix: Run `ip link set eth2 up` on leaf_router_0_0. Once the
interface comes UP, the connected route is installed, BGP advertises
10.0.0.0/24 to the spines, and full connectivity is restored for pc_0_0.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly blames leaf_router_0_0 and states both spines are fully operational with established BGP and correct forwarding, thereby rejecting the ticket's spine-failure hypothesis.
Recommends bringing eth2 up on leaf_router_0_0 with `ip link set eth2 up`, which matches the expected remediation.

The investigator's observations in the log (missing connected 10.0.0.0/24 on leaf_router_0_0, eth2 reported link-down, BGP network configured but not advertised, pc_0_0 NIC up, fabric/spines reachable) directly support the conclusion that the host-facing interface on leaf_router_0_0 is down and is the root cause; reasoning correctly links interface-state → absent connected route → no BGP advertisement and exonerates the spine.
